answer: A volcano erupts when hot rising magma and its dissolved gas build up more pressure than the rock above can hold, so the top of the pipe blows open.
summary: One cutaway volcano stays big in the middle of the frame. Its glowing chamber slowly fills and heats up, bubbles form in the magma and push it up the pipe, and a pressure gauge swings into the red as the analogy. Then the pipe blows open and lava sprays high, fades, and leaves a calm cone with a new small island. The temperature shows as text on screen while it is said, and the picture ends with the chamber glowing again as the viewer is asked to comment.

scenes.idea: Opening: the big cutaway volcano shows the hidden chamber under the cone and the question of why it erupts.
The chamber fills with hot magma, the thermometer rises to about 1000 degrees, the magma rises, pressure builds, gas bubbles form and push magma up the pipe.
The pressure cooker analogy: a big gauge whose needle climbs into the red, with the volcano small behind it.
The pipe blows open, lava sprays high, the eruption fades, and new land forms.
Closing: the chamber heats and fills again while the viewer is asked which part surprised them, the heat or the gas.

ending.tail: In the 2.5 seconds of silence the chamber keeps glowing and its bubbles keep rising slowly, then it settles calm and glowing, never cut off.

notes: S8 (story): S8 "The magma also holds dissolved gas, locked in like the fizz in a bottle.": the gas is shown by a small particles prop beside the chamber, not inside the magma, so the dissolved idea is only suggested. Fix: Optional: place the bubbles inside the chamber magma.
S10 (story): S10 "Think of a pressure cooker...": a gauge stands in for the cooker; no cooker is drawn. Fix: Optional: none needed, the needle carries the analogy.
